   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  FIRE DEPARTMENT

  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison/ Health and Human Relations Commission
  Committee

FROM:  Gregory Barton, Fire Chief

DATE:  January 27, 2026

SUBJECT:  2025 Health and Safety Commission Accomplishments

Helena M. Rosenthal, MBA, MPH, and Erica Felsenthal, PhD, have served as the Chair and
Vice Chair of the Health and Safety Commission from January 2025 to December 2025.

The areas of interest for 2025 included:
  • Mental Health
  • Emergency Preparedness
  • Wellness
  • Optimize Public Health and Safety
  • Beverly Hills Climate Action and Adaptation Plan
  • Smoking Education, Outreach and Cessation
  • Community Engagement
  • Support City Health and Safety Programs

During this time, the Health and Safety Commission accomplished the following:

  1. Held the 2nd annual Social Media Safety Day discussion to build awareness about the
  mental health effects of social media on children and their families. A Dedication to
  Social Media Safety – A special discussion, in lieu of a public meeting, led by Jane
  Tavyev Asher, MD, Cedars-Sinai, Pediatric Neurology. In 2024 the Commission
  spearheaded a City proclamation which was established on September 4, 2024,
  declaring Social Media Safety Day every year on September 4th.

  2. City of Beverly Hills Mayor and City Council recognized the Health and Safety
  Commission at the August 19, 2025, formal session for Social Media Safety, a Mayor
  initiative titled Moment of Unity.

  3. Held the 3rd annual Beverly Hills Day of Wellness event in collaboration with the Human
  Relations Commission and the Recreation and Parks Commission.

  4. Supported mental health, emergency preparedness, and wellness; addressed a topic at
  the Health and Safety Commission meeting through discussions, educational
  information, and mindfulness exercises.

  5. Provided Blue Can emergency water at a reduced cost for the Beverly Hills community
  as a continued Health and Safety Initiative from 2024.
 6. Provided fire extinguishers at a reduced cost for the Beverly Hills community as a
  continued Health and Safety initiative from 2023.

7. Conducted community outreach via social media, with the City’s Communications Office,
  promoting the guest speakers who presented at this year’s Health and Safety
  Commission meetings.

8. Maintained the resources page on the Health and Safety Commission webpage that
  provides a directory of a variety of helpful services.

9. Vice Chair Felsenthal’s and Commissioner Hilborne’s involvement in the Community
  Advisory Committee (CAC) for the City's Climate Action and Adaptation Plan (CAAP)
  aiming at helping the community come up with measures to reduce the City's
  greenhouse gas emissions and manage the future effects of climate change. The Plan
  was adopted by the City Council in April 2025.

10. Continued learning about health and safety, mental health and emergency preparedness
  related topics, programs, presentations, outreach, and education.

  January  Beverly Hills Public Works Department. An update about the
  Department’s response to the red flag warnings and windstorms and the
  City’s water supply, provided by Director of Public Works Shana Epstein.

  Nurturing a Proactive Approach for Longevity. A presentation about
  optimizing your well-being by double board-certified physician Dr. Jeffrey
  Egler.
  February  Health Care Rights and Education – A presentation by Stephanie Fajuri,
  Health Insurance Counseling and Advocacy Program (HICAP) Program
  Director, Staff Attorney, Center of Health Care Rights on helping older
  adults, people with disabilities and their caregivers navigate Medicare and
  get the health care they need.
  March  Mobile Stroke Unit – A presentation by May Nour, MD, PhD, on UCLA
  Health's Mobile Stroke Unit program.
  April  Pregnancy, Birth, Postpartum Health and Education – A presentation
  by Sarah Lavonne, Founder of Birth Bundle, Board-Certified Labor &
  Delivery Nurse, Certified Childbirth Educator, Certified Lactation Educator.
  May  Policing with Cutting-Edge Technology – A presentation by the Beverly
  Hills Police Department on utilizing advanced technology to improve
  safety.
  June  Cybersecurity Awareness Month – A presentation about online safety
  by Marc Berkman, CEO of the Organization for Social Media Safety.

  Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone Maps – A presentation by the
  Beverly Hills Fire Department on the Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone
  Map update.

  Honoring Outgoing Health and Safety Commissioner Kirk Y. Chang
  MD.

  2 of 11
   August  Recalibrating the Nervous System and Increasing Resiliency – A
  presentation by Dr. Bonnie Goldstein, LCSW, EdM, PhD, the Maple
  Counseling Center.

  2024 Water Quality Report – A presentation by the Public Works
  Department, Water Quality Specialist Jason W. Dyogi, on the 2024 Water

   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison/ Health and Human Relations Commission
  Committee

FROM:  Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services Department

DATE:  January 27, 2026

SUBJECT:  2025 Human Relations Commission Accomplishments

Vered Elkouby Nisim, and Rose Kaiserman, have served as the Chair and Vice Chair of the
Human Relations Commission from January 2025 to December 2025.

The following summary outlines the key accomplishments, community initiatives, and Work Plan
priorities advanced by the Beverly Hills Human Relations Commission (HRC) throughout
calendar year 2025. These highlights reflect activities documented in Commission meetings and
City-supported programming.

2025 Kindness Week (February 9 – 15)
  • Launched the week with a Farmers’ Market donation drive, collecting items for Foster
  Love, Midnight Mission, Safe Parking LA, Step Up on Second, Los Angeles Animal
  Services, and Westside Food Bank.
  • Supported the BHAAC Valentine’s Day Dance at Roxbury Park, promoting
  intergenerational connection.
  • Partnered with the Beverly Hills Public Library to feature kindness-themed Story Time
  and reading lists.
  • Supported Walk to School activities with BHUSD elementary schools to promote
  kindness and safety.
  • Engaged older adults through BHAAC Valentine’s programming.
  • Promoted daily social media kindness challenges, encouraging residents to
  participate in acts of kindness throughout the week.
  • Reinforced the Commission’s mission to promote civility, compassion, and positive
  human relations.
  • Supported the Kindness Van activation at Beverly Hills High School, engaging
  students directly in kindness messaging, peer-to-peer encouragement, and campus-
  wide positivity efforts. (postponed to March 26)
  • Initiated early planning for 2026 Kindness Week (Feb 8–14) with a focus on
  partnerships, scheduling, and expanded community participation.

Beverly Hills Reads!
  • Supported and highlighted the 2025 Beverly Hills Reads! community event held on
  August 24, 2025, at El Rodeo Auditorium.
  • Featured Isola by Allegra Goodman, fostering community dialogue and literacy
  engagement.
   •  Expanded outreach through collaboration with residents, students, and City departments
  to increase participation and visibility.

Day of Wellness
  • Supported the 2025 Day of Wellness on September 14, 2025, at Roxbury Park.
  • Highlighted diverse wellness sessions and strong vendor participation, with more than
  40 participating organizations.
  • Strengthened community awareness of local health and wellness resources through
  broad public engagement.

Embrace Civility Award
  • Received and reviewed 21 nominations for the 2025 Embrace Civility Award.
  • Selected an honoree and advanced recommendation for City Council recognition
  (October 28, 2025).
  • Recognized Dr. Stephen J. Jacobs for his longstanding leadership with Boy Scouts
  Troop 110 and his commitment to fostering inclusive youth engagement and community
  service.

Kindness Matters Recognition & Community Impact
  • Continued year-round recognition of individual acts of kindness by community members
  and City staff.
  • Highlighted student and youth contributions as part of the Commission’s commitment to
  fostering a respectful and inclusive community culture.
  • Highlighted individual acts of kindness through Kindness Matters recognition, including
  community and City staff contributions.
  • Recognized student and youth community participation as part of the Commission’s
  commitment to building a respectful, inclusive, and engaged Beverly Hills community.

Community Collaboration & Priority Agency Updates
  • Received public safety and community engagement updates from the Beverly Hills
  Police Department (BHPD), including crime trend reporting, youth safety initiatives, and
  seasonal security planning.
  • Reviewed outreach and education efforts tied to youth engagement, including programs
  and partnerships supporting safe and connected student experiences.
  • Received Beverly Hills Unified School District (BHUSD) updates, including district-wide
  programs, pathways, and community-facing initiatives supporting students and families.

Commission Milestones & Transition
  • Supported the City Council process to merge the Human Relations Commission with the
  Health & Safety Commission, creating the new Health and Human Relations
  Commission.
  • The merger and new Commission structure took effect in January 2026, expanding the
  City’s advisory focus to include community health, safety, and human relations while
  continuing the core values of inclusion, civility, and community connection.
  • Acknowledged and celebrated key City leadership and service milestones mentioned
  during 2025 meetings, including staff recognition and departmental transitions.

Staff would like to commend the Human Relations Commission for its outstanding achievements
and extensive accomplishments that supported the mission of the Commission.

  FIRE DEPARTMENT

  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison/ Health and Human Relations
  Commission Committee

FROM:  Gregory Barton, Fire Chief

DATE:  January 27, 2026

SUBJECT:  Discussion of 2026 Incoming Chair’s Focus Area Topics, Areas of Interest,
  and Work Plan Initiatives

ATTACHMENTS  None

The purpose of this memo is to request review and approval by the Beverly Hills City Council
Liaison/Health and Human Relations Commission Committee, consisting of Councilmember
John Mirisch and Councilmember Lester Friedman, of the Health and Human Relations
Commission (Commission) calendar year 2026 work plan.

BACKGROUND
It has been the practice of the Commission that the incoming Chair names an Area of Focus for
their term and that they provide suggestions and seek input on other Items of Interest the
Commission may want to cover or highlight in the coming year. This format was designed by the
previous Commissioners to establish a map or guideline for the Commission to follow that
provides a clear direction and focus and allows the Chair to highlight a specific topic. Also
historically, in December the Commission identifies a work plan item to be included in the
budget. The definitions appear below.

  Area of Focus:
  One umbrella topic the Chair would like the Commission to focus on during their term.

  Items of Interest:
  Subject matter/topics of interest to the Commission. Commission may want to study or
  have a staff member, or a subject area expert or a community member provide
  information to the Commission or public.

  Work Plan Items:
  An actual task that will be completed by the Health and Human Relations Commission.
  This is reflected in the City’s budget and is based on the fiscal year.

Commissioners provide input and seek approval for any other areas of interest to be heard in
2026.
 DISCUSSION

For 2026, incoming Commission Chair Rose Kaiserman requested the following area of focus
and corresponding items of interest:

FOCUS: Optimizing Mental and Physical Health, Safety, and Human Relations

  A. Create a space to cultivate best practices in optimizing health, safety, and human
  relations to continue to foster a cohesive engagement plan for the community. Support
  staff in championing issues by leveraging the commitment and engagement of various
  programs including the Just in Case Beverly Hills and Neighborhood Watch programs.

ITEMS OF INTEREST:

The following are items of interest for the Commission.
  1) Expand education and programs in the Beverly Hills community to address challenges
  experienced by individuals struggling with mental health.
  2) Public health preparedness for future health and safety challenges.
  3) Further develop and disseminate a “Mental Health First Aid Cabinet”, including
  promotion of mindfulness and mental health tools within the community by utilizing City
  platforms. Strengthening partnerships with mental health providers in the.
  4) Highlight community health, mental health, and the unhoused services for the
  community.
  5) Promote a civil environment where respect and responsible actions prevail.
  6) Raise social media safety and empower the community with the tools to stay safe and
  smart online.
  7) Emergency preparedness, communications, alerting, and drills.

  A. Topics will rotate monthly, every other month and quarterly. A schedule will be set
  accordingly. On other occasions we plan to coordinate with existing “awareness” months
  to learn about preventative health strategies. For example, if October is Breast Cancer
  Awareness month, we would have a speaker to go with that topic.

Work Plan Items for FY 2025-2026 and FY 2026-2027 (Budget)

  •  Continue to support staff and the various health, safety, and human relations related
  programs offered to the community.

RECOMMENDATION
